verdicts.reason: A wraps the headline onto two lines and leaves 'botanicals' cramped. The can is shrunk and pulled out of its circle, and the circle is cut off at the right edge with the NEW VIDEO badge stuck onto the fragment. B has the same problems: the can is separated from the circle, the circle is cropped and the badge sits on the stub. But B sets the headline on one strong line, lines the subcopy up under it and gives the logo a readable size, so its hierarchy is clearly cleaner.

A runs logo, then can, then a two-line headline, which is a sensible order. Its flaws are a cramped wrapped headline, a cut-off circle with the badge on top, and a can too small to read. B has the stronger one-line headline on the left, but it moves the logo to the far right, inside the cropped circle, where it collides with the circle and is jammed against the edge. B's badge also floats in the middle with no link to anything, so the brand mark is close to lost and the layout reads backwards.
